issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents: the problem statement and UML specify a parameterless method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, and the template leaves a TODO for implementing that method. The solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter. This parameter mismatch between the solution (boolean parameter) and the problem statement/UML/template (no parameter) will cause confusion and test failures because automated tests and students will expect a parameterless method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Preferred fix: change the solution to provide a parameterless method matching the specification, e.g. add/replace with: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; } (you may keep the boolean variant as an overload if desired: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) { return includeGuests ? numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents : numberOfInscribedStudents; }). Alternative: if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, UML diagram, and template TODO to require getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests): int and explain the parameter meaning so all artifacts match.

issues.description: The exercise and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents() (problem_statement.md calls it getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int), but the solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). Template contains a TODO for the total-students method but no implementation. This creates a naming/signature mismatch: students are instructed to implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters, yet the reference solution exposes getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean) and calls it with a boolean in dependent methods (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor). A student following the task will not find the expected no-arg method in the solution and may be confused about the intended API and return behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to implement a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total students (numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents). Then update dependent methods in the solution to call getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no parameter). Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is desired pedagogically, update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests): int and describe the parameter; but option A (no-arg method) is recommended to match the current UML and task text.
